# Julie v7.12.2

Source: https://github.com/anortham/julie/blob/main/docs/release-notes/v7.12.2.md

# Julie v7.12.2

Patch release with two correctness fixes: the stale-binary daemon restart no
longer force-aborts live MCP sessions, and the file watcher no longer silently
drops delete/rename events when the workspace lives under a symlinked path.

No user-facing tool semantics changed. No configuration changes required.
Workspace indexes from v7.12.x do not require rebuild.

## Bug Fixes

### Daemon: stale-binary restart stops force-aborting live sessions (`fb8d5797`)

The stale-binary auto-restart fired its shutdown the instant `restart_pending`
was armed — `mark_restart_pending` signaled the restart channel on the first
request regardless of how many sessions were connected. With a live session,
that bridged straight into `shutdown()`'s 60s drain, which waits for the session
count to reach zero (i.e. for clients to disconnect). Long-lived MCP sessions
don't disconnect during a daemon-initiated restart, so the drain always timed
out and **force-aborted the live session, writing a recovery marker every time**
(the observed `count=18` recovery-marker storm).

The fix is *defer + reap*:

- `mark_restart_pending` now signals the restart channel only when
  `active_sessions == 0`. Arming with live sessions just sets the latch; the
  disconnect handler re-fires the restart at `remaining == 0` — the documented
  "exit after the last session disconnects" moment.
- A new **restart-scoped session idle-reaper** bounds the leaked-session case the
  prior 2026-05-17 hang-guard worried about: while a restart is pending, sessions
  idle past `session_idle_timeout()` (default 300s, override with
  `JULIE_DAEMON_SESSION_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECS`) are evicted, and the restart fires
  once the count hits zero — without force-aborting.
- Each session now tracks `last_activity`, touched on every request and
  notification, so an actively-used session is never reaped.

`SIGTERM` / `julie-daemon stop` semantics are unchanged — an operator-initiated
stop still drains and (on timeout) force-aborts as before. Only the
*self-initiated stale-binary restart* defers instead of force-aborting.

### Watcher: stop dropping delete/rename events under symlinked roots (`e1072f20`)

The watcher's path filtering relativized event paths with a naive
`path.strip_prefix(workspace_root)`. On macOS, `notify`/FSEvents reports the
**canonical** event path (e.g. `/private/tmp/proj/...`) even when the workspace
is registered under a **symlinked** root (`/tmp/proj/...`, since `/tmp` →
`/private/tmp`). `strip_prefix` then fails, and the directory-blacklist check
fell back to inspecting the *absolute* path — whose ancestor component `tmp`
matches the blacklist — so delete/rename events for now-gone files were silently
dropped. The result: orphaned symbols and embeddings lingering in the index for
files that were actually deleted or moved. This affects any workspace located
under a symlinked path, not only temp dirs.

The fix adds `paths::relative_within_workspace(path, root)`, a symlink-tolerant
strip (direct strip → canonicalize the root and retry → canonicalize the
candidate and retry). Canonicalizing the *root* recovers the relative path even
for a deleted leaf, because only the root needs to still exist. It is wired into
all three filtering sites (directory blacklist, gitignore, deletion gitignore).
The duplicated Windows `\\?\` UNC-prefix stripping was lifted to a shared
module-level helper.

## Tests

- New unit tests in `src/tests/core/paths.rs` for `relative_within_workspace`,
  using an **explicit symlink** so the symlinked-root coverage is deterministic
  across platforms (independent of whether `/tmp` happens to be a symlink).
- The three previously-failing watcher event-queue tests are now green and serve
  as the end-to-end regression guard:
  `test_remove_event_queued_for_deleted_file`,
  `test_rename_any_nonexistent_path_emits_deleted`,
  `test_queue_atomic_save_coalesces_delete_then_modify`.
- Daemon lifecycle/session/restart tests revised to assert **clean reaping** (no
  recovery marker) instead of force-abort.

## Verification

- `cargo xtask test dev` on the v7.12.2 release tree: **34 buckets passed in
  519.3s**.
- `cargo xtask test reliability` (daemon + workspace-init + integration): all
  green (134.9s).
- Targeted: watcher + paths suites 80/80; daemon lifecycle 26/26, session 3/3,
  restart_listener 3/3.

## Upgrade Notes

- No configuration changes required. No CLI flags removed or renamed. No MCP tool
  signatures changed.
- Workspace indexes from v7.12.x do not require rebuild. If a v7.12.1-or-earlier
  daemon ran against a workspace under a symlinked path, a deleted/renamed file
  may have left a stale index entry; it will be reconciled on the next catch-up
  scan, or you can force a rebuild with `manage_workspace operation=index
  force=true`.
- New optional env var: `JULIE_DAEMON_SESSION_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECS` (default 300)
  controls how long an idle session is kept while a stale-binary restart is
  pending before it is reaped.

## Release Artifacts

- `julie-v7.12.2-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz`
- `julie-v7.12.2-x86_64-apple-darwin.tar.gz`

# Julie v7.13.0

Cross-language extraction enrichments for the Miller bridge. This minor
release lands three new extraction capabilities — C# attribute
annotations, ordered generic type-argument capture, and carrier-gated
string-literal capture — plus test-role classification on the extract
and watcher paths, a batch of per-language extractor fixes, and a new CI
gate over the full per-language extractor suite.

**Contract move:** schema `26 → 28`, extract contract `1 → 2`. This is the
release Miller re-pins to as `(28, 2)` at its M4 resolver milestone. It is
the only release whose extract contract is `2` and schema is `28`; the
batch is shipped as a single coordinated step so no intermediate
`(27, 1)` / `(26, 2)` pair ever escapes.

## Highlights

- **Generic type-argument capture (schema 27, `type_arguments` table).**
  Use-site generic type arguments are now captured with order and
  nesting preserved (`IRepository<User>` no longer collapses to
  `IRepository`). Rolled out across **all generic-bearing languages**, not
  just the C#/TS/Python that seeded it — the cross-language parity
  mandate is enforced in the plan ledger.
- **String-literal call-arg capture (schema 28, `literals` table,
  contract → 2).** Carrier-gated string literals passed to call sites are
  now persisted end-to-end. Coverage spans **26 applicable languages**
  (8 verified-not-applicable, recorded in the breadth ledger): Python,
  C#, TS, JS, Vue, Go, Ruby, Java, PHP, Rust (call + `sqlx` macro), Dart,
  Kotlin, Scala, VB.NET, Razor, GDScript, Lua, Elixir, Swift, R, C, C++,
  Zig, QML, Bash, PowerShell. Includes TS↔JS HTTP-client carrier parity
  (`ky`/`got`/`ofetch`) and Bash/PowerShell interpolation normalization.
- **C# attribute annotations on every symbol kind (Phase 1).** Type and
  member attributes (`[Table]`, `[Route]`, `[Column]`, `[Key]`,
  `[JsonProperty]`, …) are now emitted as `symbol_annotations` rows on
  fields, events, constants, properties, delegates, destructors, and the
  rest — previously only methods and constructors carried them, and every
  other kind silently dropped its attributes.
- **Test-role classification on extract + watcher paths.** Symbols are
  classified by test role at extraction time, with base-type
  test-container detection, a canonical `base_types` signal, framework
  arms, and a shared call-style core. Cross-language call-style
  materialization covers C/C++/Lua/R/Elixir; a centralized
  `classify_call_exact` matcher backs the Wave-3 adapters and closes the
  qualified-callee false-positive class.
- **New `extractor-units` CI gate.** The 2291-test per-language extractor
  suite now runs under a dedicated bucket in the **dev** and **full**
  tiers. Previously this suite ran in no bucket, so 24 pre-existing
  per-language failures were invisible to the tiers — all 24 are fixed
  and the suite is green.

## Fixes

- **24 pre-existing per-language extractor failures** repaired (surfaced
  once the suite was gated), plus a further 11 per-language extraction
  bugs fixed in the test-role pass.
- **C++ pointer/reference-return free functions** are now extracted as
  symbols instead of being skipped.
- **QML** `PropertyAnimation` binding keys are no longer miscounted as
  `Property` symbols.
- **VB.NET literal carriers** now actually load — `vbnet.toml` is embedded
  so the `[literal_carriers]` config ships with the binary.
- **Workspace root discovery** now stops the upward walk at **all** VCS
  roots (`.git`, `.hg`, `.svn`, …), not just `.git`. This fixed the
  non-hermetic `tools-workspace-targeting` rebind tests (#33) and
  hardened root resolution for non-git checkouts.
- Addressed extraction-enrichment review findings.

## Miller / consumer compatibility

Miller gates its read layer on `(schema_version, extract_contract_version)`
with exact equality. The pairing for this release is:

| Signal | Value |
|--------|-------|
| `LATEST_SCHEMA_VERSION` | **28** (027 = `type_arguments`, 028 = `literals`) |
| `EXTRACT_CONTRACT_VERSION` | **2** |

Consumers pinned to `(26, 1)` (v7.12.2) will correctly reject this release
until they re-pin to `(28, 2)`. Per Miller's plan that is a one-line
change at M4; these enrichments do not block earlier Miller milestones.

# Julie v7.13.1

Source: https://github.com/anortham/julie/blob/main/docs/release-notes/v7.13.1.md

# Julie v7.13.1

Windows daemon and adapter hardening. This patch release fixes the
overnight adapter hang, converges the adapter↔daemon version gate so two
client versions can no longer flap the shared daemon, repairs Windows
path normalization and singleton-lock detection, fixes a workspace
implicit-index regression that could fragment the index, and corrects a
line-mode scoped-filter miss. It also batches Tantivy commits and makes
the `xtask` test harness behave on Windows.

**No contract change.** Schema stays at **28**, extract contract at **2**
(unchanged from v7.13.0). Miller and other consumers pinned to `(28, 2)`
need no re-pin. This release is purely runtime/correctness fixes — no
extraction-output changes.

## Highlights

- **The all-night hang is fixed.** When the adapter lost its connection to
  the daemon mid-request (stale-binary restart, daemon crash, transport
  drop), in-flight tool calls could hang forever — a tool call left running
  overnight would still be waiting in the morning. The adapter now answers
  **every** orphaned in-flight request: idempotent calls are requeued and
  replayed against a fresh daemon, and non-idempotent calls get a synthesized
  JSON-RPC lost-connection error so the client unblocks instead of hanging.
  (`src/adapter/forwarder.rs`, `answer_orphaned_in_flight`.)
- **Version-gate convergence (no more daemon flap).** When a connecting
  adapter reports a different version than the running daemon, the gate now
  converges on a single winner instead of letting each side restart the daemon
  into its own version (the v7.12.1-adapter ↔ v7.12.2-daemon flap). A **newer**
  adapter restarts the stale daemon (converges upward); an **older** adapter is
  rejected via the new `RejectStaleAdapter` action — the daemon keeps running
  at its newer version and the stale client must be relaunched to upgrade.
  (`src/daemon/lifecycle.rs`.)
- **Windows singleton-lock detection.** The daemon's single-instance guard now
  recognizes `ERROR_LOCK_VIOLATION` (raw OS error **33**) as a lock conflict,
  not just `WouldBlock` — Windows reports `LockFileEx` contention with code 33,
  so the previous check could miss a live daemon and mis-handle startup.
  Shutdown-event signaling tightened alongside it. (`src/daemon/singleton.rs`.)
- **Windows path normalization fallback.** `to_relative_unix_style` now falls
  back to a case-insensitive, separator-agnostic string comparison when
  `Path::strip_prefix` fails on a drive-letter/case mismatch or a `\\?\` UNC
  vs. plain-path mismatch. Previously such mismatches dropped a raw absolute
  path into the database instead of a workspace-relative one. The same fallback
  is mirrored in the `julie-extractors` crate, and `base/span.rs` now routes
  through `to_relative_unix_style` with explicit `Ok`/`Err` handling instead of
  an absolute-path shortcut. (`src/utils/paths.rs`,
  `crates/julie-extractors/src/utils/paths.rs`.)
- **Implicit-index subdirectory regression fixed.** A daemon or handler rooted
  at a project **subdirectory** (e.g. started from `<project>/src/...`) running
  an implicit `index` (no explicit path) now walks up to the marked project
  root via workspace markers, instead of indexing the subdir as if it were the
  whole workspace — which fragmented the index and broke cross-file navigation
  for the rest of the project. Explicit-path and non-primary-target routing are
  unchanged; only the implicit case was affected. (`src/tools/workspace/commands/index.rs`.)
- **Line-mode scoped-filter miss fixed.** Scoped line-mode searches
  (`file_pattern` / language filters) could miss in-scope results hiding behind
  many high-scoring out-of-scope files. The candidate hard cap is raised to
  2000 and the fetch loop now tracks true candidate-window saturation
  (`LineModeCandidateWindow`) rather than inferring it from result-count, so the
  second-pass widening fires when it should. (`src/tools/search/line_mode.rs`.)

## Fixes

- **Tantivy commit batching.** Projection writes now use `commit=false` and let
  a single `release_writer()` perform one commit, instead of committing on each
  projected document — fewer fsyncs per projection. The file watcher continues
  to commit per file so live edits remain immediately searchable.
  (`src/search/projection.rs`, `src/watcher/runtime.rs`.)
- **xtask test harness on Windows.**
  - New `xtask/src/process.rs` `manifest_command` replaces `cmd /C` for
    invoking nextest with filter expressions, so filterset syntax no longer gets
    mangled by `cmd.exe` quoting.
  - Buckets whose tests are all `cfg(unix)` no longer fail the Windows run with
    nextest's empty-selection exit code 4 — they pass via `--no-tests pass`.
  - Per-bucket timeouts and concurrency (`-j 1` serialization) recalibrated for
    Windows so legitimate runs stop timing out. (`xtask/test_tiers.toml`,
    `xtask/src/runner.rs`, `xtask/src/changed.rs`.)
- **Test hermeticity.** `test_resolve_workspace_root_canonicalizes` now uses a
  real `tempfile::tempdir()` instead of the hardcoded `/tmp` (which resolved to
  `C:\tmp` on Windows and panicked in `canonicalize().unwrap()` on a clean box
  or CI). Added Windows path-fallback unit tests (case-mismatch and
  path-equals-root-modulo-case) in both `src/utils/paths.rs` and the extractor
  crate. (`src/tests/cli_tests.rs`.)

## Miller / consumer compatibility

| Signal | Value |
|--------|-------|
| `LATEST_SCHEMA_VERSION` | **28** (unchanged) |
| `EXTRACT_CONTRACT_VERSION` | **2** (unchanged) |

No schema or extract-contract change in this release. Consumers already on
`(28, 2)` (v7.13.0) require no action.

## Test evidence

- **Implicit-index regression (TDD):**
  `test_manage_workspace_implicit_index_from_subdir_resolves_to_project_root`
  written first and confirmed **RED** — pre-fix it resolved
  `…\workspace\src\nested` (the subdir) instead of `…\workspace` (the project
  root). After removing the `!explicit_path_requested` short-circuit it is
  **GREEN**.
- **No regression in workspace routing:** full
  `tests::tools::workspace::refresh_routing` module **10/10 passed**, including
  the explicit-subdir guard
  (`test_manage_workspace_index_subdirectory_under_current_root_stays_primary`)
  and all rebound/reference force/non-force cases.
- **Branch gate:** `cargo xtask test changed` mapped the diff to 17 buckets
  (cli, core, extractors, projection, get-context, and the search family).
  **16 passed**; the lone red was
  `content_scoring_tests::content_hits_have_nonzero_scores_sorted_by_score` in
  `tools-search-format-quality`. Root-caused as **pre-existing, load-induced
  flakiness — not a branch regression**: the test file and the `search_ready`
  reader-readiness gate (B-I6) are unchanged on this branch, the only
  `src/search/` change is the gate-neutral projection commit-batching, and the

# Julie v7.13.2

External extract contract release for Miller.

## Why This Release Exists

Miller now consumes Julie through `julie-server extract` as a pinned,

enough for Miller to reject incompatible indexes before it serves stale or
misread data.

- `extract_contract_version`: `3`
- `schema_version`: `28`
- `hash_algorithm`: `blake3`

Miller pins this exact pairing:

```text
julie-server v7.13.2
schema_version = 28
extract_contract_version = 3
hash_algorithm = blake3
```

Consumers pinned to contract `2` should reject this release until they are
updated to understand `hash_algorithm`.

## Notes

This is a contract metadata release. It does not change Julie's source parsing
or schema shape from the v7.13.x line.

# Julie v7.13.3

Source: https://github.com/anortham/julie/blob/main/docs/release-notes/v7.13.3.md

# Julie v7.13.3

Rescue cleanup release: Julie returns to a single `julie-server` MCP runtime,
removes the split adapter/daemon launch path, adds a dashboard launcher through
`manage_workspace`, and keeps shrinking the expensive test buckets that made
ordinary rescue work too slow.

## Why This Release Exists

The v7.13.x daemon split introduced too much operational complexity for the
actual user: coding agents running Julie as an MCP server. This release removes
the stale process surfaces and makes the default runtime simpler again:
`julie-server` serves MCP in-process over stdio and elects a per-workspace
leader for writes.

## Runtime And Config Changes

- Manual MCP configs that point at a Julie binary should point at
  `julie-server` directly. Local configs or wrappers that still reference
  `julie-adapter` or `julie-daemon` must be updated.
- Plugin users should keep using the plugin launcher; the matching
  `julie-plugin` update changes that launcher to exec `julie-server`.
- Removed runtime surfaces include the forked daemon, stdio adapter, daemon PID
  and discovery files, daemon HTTP dashboard host, daemon migration helpers, and
  `julie daemon` process-management commands.
- Existing workspace data remains in the normal Julie index locations. The
  runtime change is about process ownership, not source extraction semantics.

## Dashboard

- `manage_workspace` now supports `operation: "dashboard"` from an MCP session.
  It starts the dashboard server in the background, opens the default browser,
  and returns the local URL.
- Loaded primary workspaces are now registered in the workspace registry used by
  the dashboard, so a healthy in-process MCP session no longer leaves the
  dashboard project list showing zero workspaces.
- One-shot CLI wrappers reject dashboard launch because the background server
  would be tied to a short-lived CLI process. Use `julie-server dashboard` for
  direct CLI dashboard launches.

## Test Economy

- The `xtask` test runner now splits the broad workspace and line-search
  buckets into smaller buckets so `changed` can select narrower slices.
- The rescue status docs now track the remaining runtime pressure explicitly:
  workspace indexing is still the biggest slow bucket and remains the next
  target.

## Plugin Distribution

The matching `julie-plugin` update must launch `julie-server` directly from
`hooks/run.cjs`. During the first launch after upgrade, that launcher should
also stop an old extracted `julie-daemon` if one exists so Windows users do not
hit stale binary locks during re-extraction.

## Compatibility

No schema or external extract-contract change in this release.

| Signal | Value |
|--------|-------|
| `LATEST_SCHEMA_VERSION` | **28** |
| `EXTRACT_CONTRACT_VERSION` | **3** |
| `hash_algorithm` | **blake3** |

Consumers already compatible with v7.13.2's `(28, 3, blake3)` external extract
metadata do not need a schema re-pin for this release.

## Known Issues and Caveats

- **Multi-session leader election is one-shot (no live follower promotion).**
  Per workspace, the first session to acquire the leader lock owns writes and the
  file watcher; other sessions on the same workspace are read-only followers and
  cleanly refuse write tools with a clear message ("another session owns writes
  for this workspace; this is a read-only follower"). If the leader session
  exits, an already-running follower stays read-only until it is restarted —
  leadership is not re-elected live inside a running process. A freshly started
  session re-acquires the lock and reconciles. This is bounded, not a data race:
  the only effect is degraded (read-only) write availability for an existing
  follower until restart.
- **Requests are bounded, not unbounded.** Every in-process MCP read request is
  wrapped in a timeout (default 120s, override
  `JULIE_INPROCESS_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECS`, set `0` to disable) and returns a
  bounded error instead of hanging. This closes the earlier failure mode where a
  request against a freshly-opened workspace could stall a session. Repair runs
  in a non-cancellable background task so a timed-out request cannot corrupt an
  in-flight index.
- **Dashboard recovery markers are read-only legacy data.** The unclean-shutdown
  recovery-marker file is no longer written by the in-process server (recovery is
  handled by the startup reconcile). The dashboard only surfaces markers left
  behind by a pre-upgrade daemon build; on a clean in-process install the panel
  is empty by design.
- **Registry visibility is best-effort.** If the workspace registry DB cannot be
  opened (e.g. a filesystem or permission error under `~/.julie/`), the session
  logs a warning and continues with core search/navigation/edit intact; only
  dashboard/list visibility is degraded for that session.

## Operational Knobs

- `JULIE_INPROCESS_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECS` — per-request in-process deadline in
  seconds (default 120; `0` disables the ceiling).
- `JULIE_INPROCESS_EMBED_WAIT_SECS` — startup wait for the embedding provider
  before degrading to keyword-only search (default 5); the host keeps warming in
  the background for later sessions.

# Julie v7.14.0

Source: https://github.com/anortham/julie/blob/main/docs/release-notes/v7.14.0.md

# Julie v7.14.0

Maintenance release that supersedes the pulled v7.13.3 rollout. It keeps the
single `julie-server` runtime direction from v7.13.3, fixes the indexing
performance regression found after that release was drafted back, and hardens
the matching `julie-plugin` launcher so old extracted binaries do not survive a
version upgrade.

## Why This Release Exists

v7.13.3 was pulled after OpenClaw indexing exposed a scaling regression and a
plugin-cache issue made it possible for the dashboard to show an older Julie
version even when the plugin manifests had advanced. v7.14.0 is the clean
replacement release line for existing Julie users.

## Indexing Performance

- Fresh full indexing now defers secondary identifier index maintenance while
  loading large identifier batches, then restores the indexes before commit.
- Relationship-resolution disambiguation now uses exact scoped identifier
  presence instead of scanning qualified identifier prefixes and filtering the
  result set in memory.
- The indexing projection path now moves the extracted batch into projection
  instead of cloning large symbol/file/cleanup vectors.
- Projection rebuild logging now records major phase timings, which gives
  future release checks a clearer view of where large-workspace time is spent.

The OpenClaw regression that previously ran past the local 3-minute budget was
rechecked after the fix as a forced standalone index with embeddings disabled:
`13,494` files, `565,029` symbols, and `185,010` relationships completed in
`164.4s`.

## Plugin Launcher

The matching `julie-plugin` launcher now records the archive basename that
produced the extracted binary. When the plugin updates from one
`julie-vX.Y.Z-*` archive to another, the launcher re-extracts even if a cached
`bin/<target>/julie-server` file has a newer mtime.

This fixes the stale-binary failure mode seen during the pulled v7.13.3 rollout:
an old extracted `julie-server 7.13.2` could keep running and make the dashboard
show `7.13.2` while the plugin package had moved forward.

## Runtime And Compatibility

- No schema or external extract-contract change.
- Manual MCP configs should still point at `julie-server`.
- Plugin users should continue to use the plugin launcher; the launcher handles
  archive extraction and cache invalidation.

| Signal | Value |
|--------|-------|
| `LATEST_SCHEMA_VERSION` | **28** |
| `EXTRACT_CONTRACT_VERSION` | **3** |
| `hash_algorithm` | **blake3** |

Consumers already compatible with v7.13.2's `(28, 3, blake3)` external extract
metadata do not need a schema re-pin for this release.

# Julie v7.15.0

Source: https://github.com/anortham/julie/blob/main/docs/release-notes/v7.15.0.md

# Julie v7.15.0

Minor release that re-pins the `julie-extractors` dependency from v2.1.0 to
v2.4.0, picking up three upstream releases of extraction quality and file
selection fixes across all 34 languages.

## Extractor Upgrade (v2.1.0 → v2.4.0)

- **Broad language data-quality release (v2.3.0):** upstream moved from coarse
  "supported" language claims to fixture-backed, per-domain extraction
  evidence across the full language matrix. Includes stronger Ruby
  relationships, QML type evidence, Vue single-file component span fixes, and
  expanded annotation, doc-comment, literal, and source-region coverage.
- **Git-exact ignore-rule precedence (v2.4.0):** nested `.julieignore` files
  are now honored at any depth (previously capped) with the same semantics as
  nested `.gitignore`; each ignore file is anchored at its own directory
  exactly as git does, fixing root-relative pattern leaks; whitelists can no
  longer re-include files under excluded parent directories.
- **v3 extraction contract (v2.2.0/v2.2.1):** the extractor library now
  carries `structural_facts` and `complexity_metrics` domains (including
  framework-aware facts for ASP.NET minimal APIs, htmx, and Alpine). Julie
  does not yet consume these domains; they flow through the extraction
  pipeline as inert data.

## Automatic Reindex On Upgrade

`SEMANTIC_INDEX_ENGINE_VERSION` now embeds the new extraction contract
(`…source-regions-v1.structural-facts-v1.complexity-metrics-v1`), so existing
workspaces detect the stored-index mismatch and reindex automatically on first
contact with the new binary. Expect a one-time background reindex per
workspace after upgrading; search stays available during the catch-up.

## Runtime And Compatibility

- No Julie SQLite schema change and no external extract-contract change.
- Manual MCP configs should still point at `julie-server`.
- Plugin users get the paired `julie-server` and `julie-embedding-host`
  binaries as usual.

| Signal | Value |
|--------|-------|
| `LATEST_SCHEMA_VERSION` | **28** |
| `EXTRACT_CONTRACT_VERSION` | **3** |
| `hash_algorithm` | **blake3** |

Consumers already compatible with v7.14.x's `(28, 3, blake3)` external extract
surface need no changes.

## Verification

- `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` clean against the v2.4.0 pin.
- Engine-version lockstep tests green (contract-embedding regression test plus
  the stale-engine forced-reindex integration test).
- `cargo xtask test bucket extractor-dep-integration` PASS.
- `cargo xtask test changed` buckets green; warm `cargo nextest run -p
  julie-index` 377/377 PASS.
- Full dev tier `cargo xtask test dev` 27/27 buckets PASS in 365s.

## Honest Caveats

- The one API break in the upgrade (`ExtractionResults` gaining
  `structural_facts`/`complexity_metrics`) only touched the watcher's
  text-only construction site; extraction behavior for selected files is
  otherwise upstream-controlled.
- The new structural-facts and complexity-metrics data is not yet surfaced by
  any Julie tool — this release is about tracking the current extractor
  contract and its quality fixes, not new features.

# v7.8.0 — Tree-Sitter Extractor Audit Remediation

Source: https://github.com/anortham/julie/blob/main/docs/release-notes/v7.8.0.md

# v7.8.0 — Tree-Sitter Extractor Audit Remediation

**Theme:** Cross-cutting correctness wave across all 34 language extractors, capability-matrix honesty work, and rigor tests for previously unguarded contracts.

This release closes the verified findings from the historical tree-sitter extractor audit and locks the corrected behavior into exact semantic tests.

## Headline changes

### Extractor correctness across 34 languages
- **SQL** — JOIN relationships now emit edges from the enclosing FROM table to each joined table (no more self-edges). View-source and trigger-target relationships extracted from CREATE VIEW and CREATE TRIGGER. Dead synthetic external IDs (e.g. `external_users`) are no longer emitted; cross-file FK references are suppressed at the source until structured pending promotion lands. SQL relationship line numbers now follow the project's 1-based convention.
- **Data formats** — JSON doc-comment truncation no longer panics on multi-byte UTF-8 sequences crossing the truncation boundary. YAML alias resolution requires exact anchor name match (no more `*foo` matching `&foobar`). Markdown heading levels preserved in metadata; first heading wins for duplicate slugs; self-references filtered.
- **Multi-binding extraction** — Java, C#, VB.NET, Go, Bash, and Python now emit one Symbol per declarator/binding instead of collapsing to the first.
- **Identity & TypeInfo** — Symbol IDs are stable across re-extraction; TypeInfo merge no longer loses fields on union; visibility fallback uses language-specific defaults.
- **Ruby** — Property accessors and pending edges preserved; rspec test detection.
- **C / C++** — Method-call identifier normalization; relationship resolution disambiguates duplicate names; visibility tightening.
- **Visibility & doc comments** — Inner-doc support for Rust; doc-comment style detection per language.
- **Dart, R, Elixir** — Documentation harvesting and language-idiom corrections.
- **TypeScript / JavaScript** — Class/function/interface/import/identifier coverage.
- **Identifier & call coverage** — Generic args, decorators, parameters, assignments threaded across languages.
- **Vue / HTML / CSS / Razor embedded extraction** — Embedded JS/CSS now delegates to language-native extractors with full-file offsets preserved. Vue Options API methods/computed/data/props emit real symbols. Vue template extracts ref/slot/v-model symbols. CSS modern at-rules and pseudo selectors. Razor `@using` targets namespace-specific IDs.
- **Scripting** — PowerShell, Bash, Lua, GDScript modeling improvements.
- **JVM, Swift, Scala, PHP** — Idiom-level corrections.
- **Degraded parser failure** — Total tree-sitter parse failure now returns a degraded `ExtractionResults` with a parse diagnostic instead of losing the file.

### Capability-matrix honesty
The capability matrix at `fixtures/extraction/capabilities.json` now records honest documentation for every false `target_capabilities` claim. Previously, 12 languages silently lowered the support bar without explaining why; now every gap entry distinguishes:
- **Domain limitations** (e.g. "JSON has no static type system; types capability is intentionally unsupported") — permanent design choices.
- **Real TODOs** (e.g. "JSON Schema $ref relationship extraction is not yet implemented" or "SQL FK pending-promotion deferred — see sql/relationships.rs around line 115") — actionable closure language.

19 new gap entries across html, css, lua, qml, r, razor, sql, regex, markdown, json, toml, yaml.

### Resolver scoping
Rust namespace scoring for `std`, `core`, `alloc` now gates to Rust pending files and Rust candidate symbols only — TypeScript code receiving a path with `std/` no longer gets a Rust-flavored namespace boost.

Rust re-export crate-root detection anchored to workspace crate layouts instead of any path containing `<crate>/src`, preventing vendor-path false-positives.

### New regression tests
- `test_vue_identifier_extraction_parses_script_section_once` — locks down the Vue parses-once invariant (script section walked exactly once per extraction call).
- `test_data_format_relationships_have_exact_targets_or_no_edge` — JSON/TOML/YAML/Markdown relationships must have real targets or emit no edge.
- `test_capability_matrix_records_known_gaps_for_languages_with_unfixed_findings` — every false target_capability must have a matching documented gap entry.
- `test_capability_matrix_pending_claim_requires_pending_output_in_fixtures` — pending_relationships=true must have either fixture evidence or a documented gap.

## Important fixes from pre-merge review

The pre-merge review pass and an adversarial Codex review caught two material issues that landed in the final fix layer:

- **SymbolKind panic at the Tantivy boundary** — `SymbolKind::from_string` panicked on schema-evolved or corrupt rows. Replaced with `try_from_string` plus a `tracing::warn!` and `SymbolKind::Variable` fallback. A single bad row can no longer crash a search request.
- **EnumMember silent downgrade** (Codex finding) — the DB-rescue path in `content_search_with_index` was using `format!("{:?}", s.kind).to_lowercase()`, which produced `"enummember"` while `try_from_string` expects `"enum_member"`. After the panic fix, this would have silently degraded rescued EnumMember symbols to Variable. Switched to `s.kind.to_string()` (Display impl, snake_case).

## Verification evidence

- `cargo xtask test extractors`: PASS (golden + capability_matrix)
- `cargo xtask test parser-upgrade`: PASS (capabilities.json contract)
- `cargo xtask test changed` over the audit-remediation diff: 9/9 buckets PASS in 127.1s (final commit `d517eb47`)
- `cargo xtask test changed` over the missing-rigor diff: 2/2 buckets PASS in 2.0s (final commit `fab16fd4`)
- All four new regression tests PASS individually
- Codex adversarial review run on the fix-batch — caught one defect (EnumMember silent downgrade), now closed with regression test

## Honest caveats

- **Razor fragile fallback** — flagged by the multi-lane review but not addressed: the verbatim finding was lost to context compaction during review consolidation, and dispatching a fix without ground truth would have been guesswork. If the fragility surfaces in dogfood, it can be tracked separately.
- **2 of 4 Task 16 meta-tests not implemented** — `test_relationship_tests_assert_exact_source_target_kind_and_count` and `test_symbol_tests_assert_exact_name_kind_parent_and_range` would require auditing 30+ per-language test modules and are properly multi-day work; deliberately out of scope for this release.
- **9 Minor items** from the multi-lane review (style/cosmetic per language) — out of scope for this release; can be follow-ups against `main`.
- **SQL cross-file FK pending promotion is deferred** — current behavior suppresses unresolved FK targets at extraction. Capability gap entry on SQL records this with concrete required-closure language.

## Upgrade notes

No API changes. No fixture format changes that would invalidate stored indexes. Re-indexing is not required, but downstream consumers who depended on the old (broken) extractor output for any of the languages listed above will see corrected results.

## Plan and tracking

- Plan doc: `docs/plans/2026-05-06-tree-sitter-extractor-audit-remediation.md`
- Findings source: historical tree-sitter extractor audit bundle, removed after closure.
- PR: [#18](https://github.com/anortham/julie/pull/18) — merged at `0d6b2b42`

# v7.8.1 — Tree-Sitter Review-Finding Closure + Index Health Hardening

Source: https://github.com/anortham/julie/blob/main/docs/release-notes/v7.8.1.md

# v7.8.1 — Tree-Sitter Review-Finding Closure + Index Health Hardening

**Theme:** Patch release closing 12 review findings raised against the v7.8.0 tree-sitter remediation. Eight of them come from the formal review matrix (TS-RF-001..008); four more are follow-on issues caught by an adversarial Codex review on the remediation diff itself.

No API changes. No fixture format changes. No re-indexing required.

## Headline fixes

### Tree-sitter review findings (TS-RF-001..008)

Closes the eight findings tracked in `docs/TREE_SITTER_REVIEW_FINDINGS_STATUS.md` with executable evidence rather than documented gaps.

- **TS-RF-001 — relationship ID collisions.** Relationship IDs now include callsite identity (`file_path`, `line_number`) so a caller invoking the same callee on multiple lines no longer collapses to one edge.
- **TS-RF-002 — embedded child rekey.** HTML `<script>`/`<style>` and Vue style remaps refresh span-derived IDs and rekey embedded child `parent_id` pointers after host offsets are applied.
- **TS-RF-003 — Vue parses-once invariant.** Vue identifier extraction parses the SFC exactly once per pass, carries section offsets through byte and line spans, and computes containing symbols from adjusted host coordinates.
- **TS-RF-004 — `<script setup>` spans.** Variables, imports, function declarations, and standalone macro symbols inside `<script setup>` now carry exact file-relative line/byte spans with column normalization.
- **TS-RF-005 — HTML embedded body offsets.** Offsets come from the embedded text node's tree-sitter bounds instead of substring matching. Duplicate attribute text inside the host can no longer steal the span.
- **TS-RF-006 — SQL view_source / trigger_target.** SQL emits these relationships from the AST when the parser is happy and falls back to a regex matcher only on `ERROR` nodes.
- **TS-RF-007 — Regex fallback span fidelity.** Regex fallback symbols build their `NormalizedSpan` from the actual text-match range via `from_content_range` + `create_symbol_from_span`, not from the root parser node.
- **TS-RF-008 — Capability matrix requires evidence.** A previously-open SQL relationships gap can no longer disappear silently; the capability matrix now requires golden fixture evidence before allowing the entry to close.

### Index health hardening (post-review fixes)

An adversarial Codex review on the TS-RF remediation diff surfaced four follow-on issues. Closed in the same release to keep the audit trail clean.

- **B1 (HIGH) — `ProjectionFailure` invariant silently cleared.** `set_dirty_projection_count(0)` removed both `TantivyDirty` and `ProjectionFailure` together, so an abandoned file's failure indication vanished the moment any other dirty file succeeded. Introduced `abandoned_projection_files: BTreeSet<String>` in `IndexingRuntimeState`. `ProjectionFailure` now tracks that set's emptiness, not the dirty counter. The watcher records a path on abandonment and clears it on per-file recovery; `begin_operation` resets the set. Three inline regression tests cover the invariant.
- **B2 (MEDIUM) — phantom-fd detail suppressed.** `render_report` printed `"Database not initialized"` whenever `canonical_store` was `Unavailable`, swallowing the rich `"ON-DISK STATE MISSING: ...Restart daemon and force-reindex to recover."` detail string. The report now prints `canonical_store.detail` when present and falls back to the generic line only when detail is empty.
- **B3 (LOW-MED) — Vue containing_symbol_id non-determinism.** When two symbols tied on priority and size, `find_containing_symbol_id_for_span` produced different results across runs because the stable sort preserved `HashMap` iteration order. Added an `a.id.cmp(&b.id)` tiebreaker.
- **L1 (DOC) — SQL CREATE_VIEW regex CTE edge case.** On `ERROR`-node fallback, the non-greedy first-`FROM` capture in `CREATE_VIEW_SOURCE_RE` grabs CTE/subquery sources instead of the view's actual base table. Documented up-front so the trade-off is visible to readers.

## Verification evidence

Recorded on the unpushed fix commits at the time they were authored (commits `7738219d`, `069b9d76`):

- 11 targeted regression tests covering the new invariants — all green.
- 53 broader gates on touched paths — all green.
- `cargo xtask test changed` over the post-review fix-batch — 22 buckets, 544.2s, all green.
- Verification ledger: `docs/plans/2026-05-07-tree-sitter-review-findings-remediation.md`.

A fresh `cargo xtask test dev` was rerun on the v7.8.1 version-bump commit before tagging.

## Honest caveats

- **Release-daemon false deleted-file detection on connect** still wants live dogfood validation. This is a known lead behind the `Transport closed` reports observed in earlier sessions; not addressed in this patch.
- **Windows release-binary restart and replacement flow** improved structurally in earlier work but still wants live validation.

## Upgrade notes

No API, schema, or fixture changes. Existing indexes remain valid. Downstream consumers running into the bugs above (relationship-edge collisions on same-line repeated calls, Vue/HTML embedded span drift, swallowed phantom-fd diagnostics, abandoned projection files invisible in health reports) will see corrected behavior after upgrade.

# Julie v7.8.4

Source: https://github.com/anortham/julie/blob/main/docs/release-notes/v7.8.4.md

# Julie v7.8.4

Workspace-root safety hardening, faster per-tool test routing, and a docs fix
for the Codex MCP install snippet.

## Highlights

- Sensitive system paths (filesystem root, home directories, `/Users`,
  `/home`, `/root`, Windows system/user containers) are now refused at every
  workspace registration entry point — not only the process-cwd auto-binding
  path covered in v7.8.3. Daemon registry rows can no longer be created for
  these roots.
- MCP handler split into per-tool files (`src/handler/tools/<name>.rs`) so a
  one-tool edit no longer drags `cargo xtask test changed` into a full dev-tier
  fallback. Test bucket count grew 14 → 22 with finer-grained per-tool routing.
- Corrected the Codex MCP install instructions on the marketing site. The
  panel referenced a non-existent `codex mcp add julie -- node ...` command;
  it now shows the actual `~/.codex/config.toml` block users need to paste.

## Workspace-Root Safety Hardening

v7.8.3 added a sensitive-root guard for the process-cwd startup path, but
`WorkspacePool::get_or_init`, `JulieServerHandler::primary_binding_for_root`,
and the `manage_workspace` `index` / `open` / `register` commands could still
upsert sensitive roots into the daemon registry. In practice this surfaced as
`/Users/murphy` appearing as a pending registered workspace.

This release:

- Extracts the guard into `src/workspace/root_safety.rs` (single source of
  truth, separate CWD vs. generic error messages).
- Inserts the guard before any upsert/bind/index path:
  `WorkspacePool::add_workspace_root`, primary-binding canonicalization, the
  index force-reindex flow, the open-target add and existing-row branches, and
  the register/remove command.
- Adds regression test
  `test_get_or_init_rejects_sensitive_root_without_registering_row` proving the
  daemon pool refuses `/` without leaving a registry row.

## Per-Tool Test Routing

The MCP handler previously lived in a single `src/handler.rs` that the changed
selector treated as shared infrastructure — every edit to it forced
`cargo xtask test changed` to fall back to the full dev tier.

- Each of the 12 MCP tools now lives in its own
  `src/handler/tools/<name>.rs`, with a dedicated `#[tool_router]` impl block
  composed in `handler.rs`. `handler.rs` shrunk 3,254 → 2,500 lines.
- `xtask/src/changed.rs` removed `src/handler/` from `DEV_FALLBACK_PREFIXES`,
  added cross-cutting handler files to `DEV_FALLBACK_FILES` to preserve their
  fallback safety, and added 1:1 tool→bucket routing (e.g.
  `src/handler/tools/fast_search.rs` → `tools-search-*`,
  `src/handler/tools/edit_file.rs` → `tools-editing`).
- The monolithic `tools-search` and `tools-get-context` buckets were split
  into per-tool buckets. Buckets: 14 → 22; dev tier entries: 22 → 32.
- New routing tests cover handler tool dispatch, telemetry, and shared-
  infrastructure fallback (`changed_tests.rs`, `manifest_contract_tests.rs`).

The user-visible effect: tool-only edits now run a small targeted bucket set
instead of the full dev tier.

## Codex MCP Install Snippet Fix

The marketing site's Codex install panel previously showed
`codex mcp add julie -- node /path/to/julie-plugin/hooks/run.cjs`. That
command does not exist — Codex configures MCP servers via
`~/.codex/config.toml`. The panel and the copy-to-clipboard payload now show:

```toml
[mcp_servers.julie]
command = "node"
args = ["/path/to/julie-plugin/hooks/run.cjs"]
```

(The same incorrect command appeared in v7.8.3's release notes; treat the
TOML block above as authoritative.)

## Artifacts

- `julie-v7.8.4-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz`
- `julie-v7.8.4-x86_64-apple-darwin.tar.gz`
- `julie-v7.8.4-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip`
- `julie-v7.8.4-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz`

# Julie v7.8.5

Source: https://github.com/anortham/julie/blob/main/docs/release-notes/v7.8.5.md

# Julie v7.8.5

Plugin hook cleanup release. The julie-server binary is functionally
identical to v7.8.4; this version exists so users on the v7.8.4 plugin
get an update notification that delivers the hook fix.

## Why this release exists

The v7.8.4 julie-plugin shipped two PreToolUse hooks that fired globally
instead of only inside indexed Julie workspaces:

- `pretool-broad-tests.cjs` (Claude Code) — blocked unfiltered
  `cargo test --lib` / `cargo nextest run --lib` in any project the
  plugin was installed under, then suggested `cargo xtask test changed`
  as the alternative. That command only exists in the Julie repo, so
  the discipline was being projected onto unrelated cargo projects with
  no working substitute.
- `codex-pretooluse.cjs` (Codex CLI) — same blocking logic on the Codex
  side.

`pretool-agent.cjs` had the same kind of leak — emitting Julie-specific
tool guidance on every Agent call regardless of workspace — though it
only added context rather than blocking.

## Plugin changes (julie-plugin v7.8.5)

1. `pretool-broad-tests.cjs` and `codex-pretooluse.cjs` are removed.
   The narrowest-test-first discipline they enforced is documented in
   the upstream `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md` (TDD methodology + subagent
   test rules), which is the right layer for project-wide conventions.
   Hooks should be reserved for blast-radius safety, not coding
   discipline.
2. `pretool-agent.cjs` now gates on `findIndexedWorkspace(cwd)` and
   silently exits when run outside a registered Julie workspace.
3. `bin/install-codex.cjs` no longer installs a `PreToolUse` entry into
   `~/.codex/hooks.json`; `codex-sessionstart` and `codex-posttooluse`
   still install as before.

## Julie source changes

- Removed the dev-only `.claude/hooks/pretool-broad-tests.cjs` from this
  repo for symmetry with the plugin cleanup.
- Plan/design/rubric documents for the in-flight best-in-class
  tree-sitter capability program were committed earlier in the release
  cycle. These are internal planning artifacts, not user-facing API
  changes.

There are no behavioral or API changes in the julie-server binary
between v7.8.4 and v7.8.5.

## Upgrade notes

- Plugin users on v7.8.4: the Claude Code plugin updater should offer
  v7.8.5 next time you open a session that loads the plugin. Accept the
  update to get the workspace-scoped hooks.
- Codex users on v7.8.4: re-run `node bin/install-codex.cjs` in the
  refreshed plugin install. It removes the stale `PreToolUse` entry
  from `~/.codex/hooks.json` automatically (sentinel-based merge).
- Julie source consumers: no migration. The binary behavior is
  unchanged.

  - `pretool-grep-redirect.cjs` outside a registered workspace: exit 0,

# Julie v7.9.0

Source: https://github.com/anortham/julie/blob/main/docs/release-notes/v7.9.0.md

# Julie v7.9.0

Extractor trust-contract release. This version makes tree-sitter extractor
quality more explicit, adds certified symbol body spans and body hashes, and
persists those fields through Julie's storage/search surfaces for downstream
tools that need safer code-edit coordinates.

## Highlights

- New extractor contract version: `2026-05-11.body-span-v1`.
- Every applicable language now participates in the same `body_span` /
  `body_hash` contract. No language-specific edit allowlist is introduced.
- `fixtures/extraction/capabilities.json` now records
  `kind_coverage.body_spans` with `supported`, `not_applicable`, and
  `open_gaps` entries. Current body-span open gaps: `0`.
- Julie's symbol database now stores optional body span byte/line/column
  coordinates plus `body_hash`, with automatic schema migration.
- The tree-sitter certification report now includes body-span coverage and is
  backed by release-profile real-world evidence: 22 verified repos, 0 skipped.

## Body Span And Hash Contract

Julie extractors now emit optional `body_span` and `body_hash` fields for
symbols with a meaningful body.

- `body_span` is a normalized span in original source coordinates:
  1-based lines, 0-based columns, and byte offsets.
- For grammars with explicit body nodes, the span follows the tree-sitter body
  node. That means brace-delimited languages include the body delimiters when
  the grammar body node includes them; indentation-suite languages use the
  suite range.
- Leaf symbols and symbols without a replaceable body report no body span.
- `body_hash` is derived from a normalized token stream inside `body_span`, so
  whitespace-only edits do not change the hash while identifiers, literals,
  operators, comments, punctuation, and delimiters do.

This is intentionally additive. Existing consumers can ignore the new fields.
Consumers that use them should gate on `EXTRACTION_CONTRACT_VERSION` or the
capability snapshot rather than hard-coding language names.

## Extractor Capability Model

The capability matrix now distinguishes:

- `supported`: the language fixture has evidence for that kind and capability.
- `not_applicable`: the kind exists but the capability does not make sense for
  that kind, such as leaf symbols with no body.
- `open_gaps`: the kind is applicable but not yet supported.

Public body-edit support is blocked unless every applicable language has zero
body-span open gaps. This keeps all supported languages on the same functional
bar.

## Storage And Search

The SQLite schema moves to version 25 and adds nullable columns:

- `body_start_line`, `body_start_col`, `body_end_line`, `body_end_col`
- `body_start_byte`, `body_end_byte`
- `body_hash`

Symbol insertion, bulk insertion, query hydration, lightweight symbol queries,
and text-search enrichment now preserve the new fields. The semantic index
engine version includes the new extractor contract, so workspaces should be
refreshed/reindexed before depending on body-span data.

## Documentation Cleanup

Historical raw extractor review dumps under `docs/findings/` were removed.
Current truth now lives in generated capability fixtures, the certification
report, real-world evidence, and the extractor contract docs.

## Artifacts

- `julie-v7.9.0-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz`
- `julie-v7.9.0-x86_64-apple-darwin.tar.gz`
- `julie-v7.9.0-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip`
- `julie-v7.9.0-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz`

## Upgrade Notes

- Existing databases migrate automatically on open.

# Julie v7.9.2

Source: https://github.com/anortham/julie/blob/main/docs/release-notes/v7.9.2.md

# Julie v7.9.2

Sidecar bootstrap reliability + deferred-session workspace open fix. This
patch eliminates a thundering-herd race in the embedding sidecar bootstrap
and lets `manage_workspace(operation="open", path=...)` succeed when no
primary workspace is bound yet.

## Highlights

- **Single-flight sidecar bootstrap.** Concurrent first-run sessions on
  the same machine no longer race each other through `uv pip install
  torch` and the torch version probe. A cross-process file lock at
  `<sidecar-cache>/.julie-sidecar-bootstrap.lock` serializes the slow
  bootstrap path while leaving the fast steady-state path uncontended.
- **Deferred-session open-by-path.** When the daemon has a workspace
  pool but no primary workspace is currently bound, opening a workspace
  by path now resolves its on-disk index location directly from the
  pool's shared indexes directory instead of routing through the
  primary-anchor helper. This unblocks the deferred-session open flow.

## Sidecar Bootstrap Lock

Before this fix, every concurrent process that started bootstrap on a
machine with an unprovisioned sidecar venv could each spawn its own
`uv pip install torch==<ver>` and `python -c "import torch; ..."`
probe, producing the symptom captured in the operator log: 14+ parallel
torch installs and 10+ parallel version probes pinned to 30-40% CPU each.

The fix:

- `acquire_bootstrap_lock(&venv_path)` opens (creating if needed) a
  `.julie-sidecar-bootstrap.lock` file in the **parent** of the venv,
  then takes an exclusive `fs2` advisory lock on it.
- Placing the lock file outside the venv means `ensure_venv_exists` can
  `remove_dir_all(venv_path)` to rebuild without invalidating the lock.
- The lock spans the entire managed-bootstrap path: venv creation,
  install-marker check, sidecar editable install, optional CUDA torch
  reinstall, and torch version verification.
- Drop releases the OS lock; on process crash the kernel releases the
  lock at handle close, so a crashed bootstrap doesn't strand future
  starts.

Override paths (`JULIE_EMBEDDING_SIDECAR_PROGRAM`,
`JULIE_EMBEDDING_SIDECAR_VENV`) skip the lock and continue to behave
exactly as before.

## Deferred Workspace Open Routing

`IndexRoute::path_backed_route` now checks `handler.workspace_pool`
first. When the pool is present, on-disk paths are computed directly:

- `<pool.indexes_dir()>/<workspace_id>/db/symbols.db`
- `<pool.indexes_dir()>/<workspace_id>/tantivy`

This matches the layout that `workspace_storage_anchor`-routed lookups
produce in the pool case, but does not require a bound `current
workspace`. Stdio-mode (no pool) and override-based layouts still flow
through the existing helper and are unchanged.

## Verification

- `cargo check`
- `cargo xtask test changed`
- `cargo nextest run --lib test_managed_sidecar_bootstrap_is_serialized_across_concurrent_callers`
- `cargo nextest run --lib test_manage_workspace_open_path_succeeds_without_bound_primary_in_deferred_session`

## Artifacts

- `julie-v7.9.2-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz`
- `julie-v7.9.2-x86_64-apple-darwin.tar.gz`
- `julie-v7.9.2-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip`
- `julie-v7.9.2-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz`

## Upgrade Notes

- No schema or contract changes.
- No reindex required.
- Operators who saw the parallel `uv pip install torch` / `import torch`
  storm during a first-run on a fresh machine should observe one
  serialized bootstrap per machine going forward.

# Julie v7.9.3

Source: https://github.com/anortham/julie/blob/main/docs/release-notes/v7.9.3.md

# Julie v7.9.3

Daemon singleton hardening + auto-embedding catch-up on session connect.
This patch closes a Linux-only daemon respawn cascade that produced 577
processes and hundreds of browser tabs in a 29-second window, and fixes
a related gap where a workspace indexed before the embedding sidecar
finished bootstrapping would stay at 0 vectors indefinitely.

## Highlights

- **Stable Linux process identity.** `linux_process_creation_time` no
  longer derives its value from wall-clock arithmetic. The identity is
  now an FNV-1a hash of `/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id` plus the raw
  `/proc/<pid>/stat` starttime ticks. Both inputs are kernel-managed
  and immune to `settimeofday`, NTP step adjustments, suspend/resume,
  and VM live-migration time-warp.
- **Singleton daemon enforcement via flock.** A new
  `daemon.singleton.lock` file (never unlinked) is exclusively flocked
  for the daemon's lifetime. Acquired before PID-file creation, so any
  racer that slips past `O_CREAT|O_EXCL` is caught by a kernel-enforced
  lock and bails cleanly with "another daemon is already running for
  this JULIE_HOME".
- **Three-state PID file classifier.** `PidFile::check_running` is now a
  thin back-compat wrapper around `check_status -> PidFileStatus
  { Alive(u32) | Dead | Indeterminate }`. The launcher distinguishes
  "no daemon" from "daemon mid-write" so it never unlinks the state
  file or respawns into a racing daemon.
- **MissingEmbeddings repair reason.** When a workspace has indexed
  symbols but zero embeddings (e.g. indexed before the Python sidecar
  finished bootstrapping), `plan_primary_workspace_repair` now surfaces
  `MissingEmbeddings` instead of reporting "Index is up-to-date".
  `spawn_workspace_embedding` runs in the background once the provider
  settles, no full re-index required.

## The 577-Daemon Cascade

On Linux, `linux_process_creation_time` previously derived an absolute
epoch value from `SystemTime::now() − /proc/uptime + ticks/HZ` in f64.
`now` and `/proc/uptime` are separate syscalls and `/proc/uptime` is
only hundredths-of-a-second precise, so two calls for the same live PID
returned values that drifted by µs–ms. `check_running` did an exact
`==` comparison and **unlinked the running daemon's PID file** on
mismatch. The adapter's poll loop saw the file disappear, declared the
daemon dead, spawned another, repeated every ~50ms. In one user
report, 577 daemons spawned in 29 seconds, each auto-opening a
dashboard browser tab.

A subsequent attempt to derive boot time from `/proc/stat btime`
(`getboottime64` = `offs_real − offs_boot`) was still vulnerable to
`settimeofday`-style wall-clock steps — flagged by an adversarial Codex
review. The shipped fix uses `boot_id`, which is a UUID generated at
boot and never recomputed from the real-time clock.

Three concurrent defenses now apply:

1. **Stable identity** — `check_running` cannot misclassify a live
   daemon as PID-recycled.
2. **Singleton lock** — even if a future identity regression sneaks in,
   only one daemon can hold `daemon.singleton.lock` per JULIE_HOME.
3. **Indeterminate PID-file state** — empty PID files within a small
   freshness window are no longer treated as Dead; the launcher waits
   instead of unlinking a daemon mid-`create_exclusive`.

The singleton lock file lives at `~/.julie/daemon.singleton.lock` and
is never deleted (so the inode stays stable across process restarts).
The PID file path and format are unchanged.

## Auto-Embedding Catch-Up

`run_primary_workspace_repair` previously returned `None` ("Index is
up-to-date — no indexing needed") for any workspace whose symbols were
already on disk and whose files hadn't changed, regardless of whether
embeddings existed. If the embedding sidecar bootstrapped *after* the
initial index ran (cold-start sidecar takes 30–60s, indexing takes <5s),
the workspace would stay at 0 vectors forever — even after later
sessions saw the provider go Ready.

The fix adds an `IndexingRepairReason::MissingEmbeddings` variant.
After the existing nine repair-reason checks, when no other reason
fires AND `embedding_count == 0`, the planner pushes
`MissingEmbeddings` (unless a catch-up embedding task is already
in-flight for this workspace — checked via `handler.embedding_tasks` so
concurrent session connects don't cancel each other's work).
`run_primary_workspace_repair_body` treats `MissingEmbeddings` as a
reason that requires the embedding pipeline, so the existing catch-up
branch in `commands/index.rs` fires `spawn_workspace_embedding`.

## Adversarial Review Findings Addressed

Codex (gpt-5.5 xhigh, fresh reviewer with `--ignore-user-config
--ignore-rules`) flagged four issues during this branch's review.
Three were addressed before tagging:

- **Finding #1 (high):** `/proc/stat btime` is not invariant for the
  boot session; `settimeofday` affects it. **Fixed** — identity now
  derives from `boot_id` + raw start_ticks, no wall-clock value
  involved.
- **Finding #2 (high):** `MissingEmbeddings` could cancel its own
  in-flight repair under concurrent session connects (the second
  session sees `embedding_count == 0` because the first session's
  embedding task hasn't stored its first batch yet, then
  `cancel_primary_embedding_task` kills the running task and restarts
  from scratch). **Fixed** — planner checks
  `handler.embedding_tasks` before pushing `MissingEmbeddings`.
- **Finding #3 (medium):** A corrupt PID file with a far-future mtime
  could pin the launcher in `Starting` forever. **Fixed** —
  `is_pid_file_fresh` only accepts future mtimes within a small skew
  tolerance (5s), and `classify_legacy_or_unparseable` requires the
  content to be empty for the Indeterminate path.

**Finding #4 (medium, open):** Workspaces where every symbol is
filtered out by embedding-eligibility policy (docs/config-only) will
loop `MissingEmbeddings` every session connect, wasting ~2s per
connect. Not catastrophic; a clean fix requires a persisted
"embedding-pipeline-completed-with-N-eligibles" marker in
`embedding_config`. Tracked as a follow-up.

## Test Evidence

# v7.8.2 — Tool-output compaction, line-match correctness, plugin sync

Source: https://github.com/anortham/julie/blob/main/docs/releases/v7.8.2.md

# v7.8.2 — Tool-output compaction, line-match correctness, plugin sync

**Theme:** Quality-of-life patch release. Tool output formatters compact same-file runs (token savings for agents), `line_matches` gets a correctness fix for compound identifiers, `edit_file` learns cross-workspace targeting, and a new `cargo xtask sync-plugin` command replaces the manual skill-mirror dance for plugin distribution.

No API changes that require user action. No fixture format changes. No re-indexing required.

## Headline changes

### Tool-output compaction (token savings for agents)

`deep_dive`, `get_context` (readable + compact), `blast_radius`/impact, and `fast_search` (locations and full line mode) now group consecutive same-file hits under a single file header instead of repeating the path on every row. Pure formatting change — no semantic difference, just fewer tokens per result. Test coverage added across all five formatters.

### `line_matches` compound-identifier fix

A search for `workspace_is_primary` previously matched lines containing only an unrelated sub-token like `workspace_label:` because the tokenizer split the compound on `_` and any sub-token was treated as sufficient.

Fixed: compound terms (containing punctuation or camelCase boundaries with multiple sub-tokens) now require a contiguous case-insensitive substring match. Simple terms keep the existing tokenized matching. New `line_match_strategy_tests.rs` covers positive matches, negative matches against decomposed sub-tokens, and excluded-term semantics.

If you previously relied on the loose matching for short identifier searches, the fix tightens precision without affecting simple-token lookups.

### `edit_file` cross-workspace targeting

`edit_file` now accepts a `workspace` parameter and routes via `resolve_workspace_filter` like `rewrite_symbol`. Previously the schema rejected `workspace` due to `deny_unknown_fields`. New `test_edit_file_routes_to_target_workspace` verifies the target-workspace edit lands and the primary workspace is left untouched.

### `call_path` returns compact text instead of pretty JSON

`call_path` output now uses a compact text format (`found=… hops=… 1. A --call--> B at file`). Easier for agents to read, fewer tokens, and the structural information that matters is preserved. Internal consumers (call_path's own tests) were updated; no external Rust callers, no `.cjs` plugin scripts, and the agent-facing instructions describe the tool semantically rather than by parse format. If you were parsing `call_path` JSON in your own tooling, switch to text.

### Developer ergonomics

- **`cargo xtask sync-plugin`** — new subcommand that mirrors `.claude/skills/` from the source repo into `~/source/julie-plugin/skills/` (full mirror with deletes), and reports hook divergence without writing. Replaces the manual `cp` step previously documented for plugin-skill updates. `--dry-run` supported.
- **`cargo xtask test nano`** — new tier running `core-database` + `core-fast` only (~25s). Fastest sanity tier for the edit-test loop, sits below `smoke` and `dev`.
- **README, CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md** — Codex CLI and OpenCode plugin install paths documented.

### Cleanups

- Stranded debug artifact (`probe.cjs` in `.claude/hooks/`) removed.
- Minor clippy nit (`field_reassign_with_default`) in `xtask/src/sync_plugin.rs`.
- ~80% of the line delta in this release is `cargo fmt` reformatting in daemon, watcher, and PID files. No semantic change in those files.

## Known issues / caveats

- **Daemon force-restart can drop active MCP sessions.** When the `julie-server` release binary is rebuilt while a Claude Code session has an active MCP connection, the daemon's stale-binary auto-restart drains active sessions for 10 seconds, then force-shuts-down with `Session drain timeout exceeded, forcing shutdown — in-flight writes may be lost`. Sessions running heavy work (embeddings, indexing, large search) often can't drain in 10s. The stdio adapter does not always reconnect cleanly, and `mcp__julie__*` tools become unavailable in the affected session until restart. Tracked in `TODO.md` under "Daemon Reliability"; not addressed in this release. Workaround: avoid `cargo build --release` while a Claude Code session is open against the local `julie-server` binary, or restart the session after rebuilding.

## Verification

Pre-release code review covered all four commits (70 files, +3343/-356). No Critical or Important findings; minor cleanups applied before tagging. Test tiers run prior to tag (run by user in their own environment).

## Upgrade notes

- No fixture rebuild required.
- No re-indexing required.
- If you were parsing `call_path` JSON output in custom tooling, switch to the new compact text format.
- Plugin maintainers: `cargo xtask sync-plugin` replaces manual skill copy; existing manual workflows still work.
